title: EventStream chunk provenance and rehydration protocol
creator: Aisha Kumar
description: Problem: our current streaming API occasionally produces duplicate or partially ordered tokens after transient connection loss, and legacy clients have inconsistent handling of partial structured outputs and function/tool call boundaries. This ticket designs and implements a compact, backward-compatible event-stream message header and a client-server "rehydration" protocol to stitch event sequences after a reconnection and to preserve deterministic function-call boundaries and structured output JSON fragments. The outcome should reduce duplicate events, preserve ordering across multi-part payloads, and provide clear compatibility fallbacks for older SDKs.
decision_log: Adopt a minimal header on each event: seq (monotonic per-session), chunk_id (UUID per partial payload), origin (model variant id), token_index_start, token_index_end, checksum (CRC32) and boundary_type (partial|final|function_call|meta).

Introduce a reconnect handshake called STITCH that contains last_ack_seq and a short replay window request (max 256 events). Server will prefer delta replay by seq. If client cannot accept provenance headers, server will fall back to legacy stream mode (stream-legacy) with advisory warning meta event.

Treat function/tool call boundaries as atomic: function_call events must be emitted as their own chunk(s) with boundary_type=function_call. On replay, function_call chunks are re-delivered only if the session shows they were not acknowledged (last_ack_seq < function_call_seq).

Use an idempotency and deduplication strategy based on (session_id, seq) with a server-side dedup window of 1024 seq entries for in-memory fast-path, and longer persistence to durable store for sessions with external storage enabled (Dedicated/Private customers).

Compatibility: stream-v2 (with provenance headers) becomes default; stream-v1 remains available for 6 months behind feature flag and emits a meta advisory event at connection start advising client upgrade.
acceptance_criteria: Clients that reconnect using STITCH and provide last_ack_seq see no more than 0.1% duplicated tokens in 99% of reconnect tests (target measured over 5000 simulated reconnects).
Function-call sequences are delivered exactly-once from the perspective of application consumers in >99.9% of tests (deterministic tests + chaos tests).

Legacy clients remain supported: when a client connects in legacy mode, server emits advisory meta event and preserves existing behavior (no headers), with no increased error rate in existing test harness.
End-to-end integration tests (SDKs: JS, Python, Go) pass for partial JSON output assembly, tool call replay, and stitch-based replay scenarios.
Server-side metrics emit reconnect_rate, stitch_replays, duplicate_token_rate, and long_gap_replays; new dashboard panels created in Console.
tasks: Design event header wire format (compact JSON header per event + optional binary payload compression) - spec doc and examples.
Implement server-side seq counter and chunk_id generator; integrate with session lifecycle and persistent session store for Dedicated/Private.
Build STITCH handshake endpoint: validate last_ack_seq, compute minimal replay set, and return server_stitch_token with server_seq_highwater and any required KV-cache hints.
Implement dedup window (in-memory LRU) and durable dedup record for long-lived sessions.
Extend function/tool call emitter to mark boundary_type=function_call and include tool metadata with opaque tool_call_id for downstream idempotency.
SDK work: JS and Python client changes to support provenance headers, STITCH handshake, and partial JSON reassembly helper with checksum verification.
Create integration tests and chaos tests (connection kill at random token boundaries, delayed packets, reordered TCP segments simulation).
Update Console to show stitch_replays and per-session duplicate token rate; add alerting thresholds.
Write migration notes and compatibility guidance for customers and partner SDKs.
Security review for the STITCH token contents (no secrets in token); threat model signoff.
test_plan: Unit tests for header encode/decode with fuzzing (malformed headers, truncated payloads).
Integration harness: create a test server that intentionally drops Nth event and validate client STITCH behavior with replay window requests (0..256).
Property tests for ordering and deduplication: ensure sequence monotonicity and idempotency invariants hold over 1M generated events across varying batch sizes.
Chaos testing in dev cluster: simulate abrupt network partitions, server failover, and long-tail latencies for KV-cache; measure duplicate events and reassembly errors.
Compatibility tests: run legacy client mode against stream-v2 server and verify advisory meta event and no change in functional tests.
Load test: create 10k concurrent streaming sessions, induce reconnects in 2% of them, ensure system remains within latency SLOs and dedup window memory bounded.
rollout_plan: Feature-flag gated rollout: start with internal canary (5% of sessions) with stream-v2 enabled and detailed logging for stitch flows.
Expand to early access customers and SDK beta testers (two-week window) and collect metrics and bug reports.
Gradual ramp to 50% with automated guardrails (duplicate_token_rate < 1% and stitch_replay_success_rate > 99%).
After two weeks of stability, enable stream-v2 for all hosted sessions and schedule deprecation path for stream-v1 (6 months notice).
